lines.title: Main Line: ...dxc4 ...Bf5
lines.pgn: 1. d4 d5 2. c4 c6 3. Nf3 Nf6 4. Nc3 dxc4 5. a4 Bf5 6. e3 e6 7. Bxc4 Bb4 8. O-O O-O 9. Qe2 Nbd7
lines.lineSummary: The main line Slav with ...Bf5 — Black develops the light-squared bishop before ...e6, the key Slav idea.
lines.strategicGoal: Take on c4 to develop ...Bf5 BEFORE ...e6. This solves the QGD's main problem of the bad bishop.
lines.commonOpponentMistake: White plays a4 but Black already has ...Bf5 out, so the bishop is active.
lines.punishmentIdea: With ...Bf5 already developed, Black has solved the light-square problem. ...e6 and ...Bb4 follow.
lines.hintText: The whole point of the Slav: take on c4, play ...Bf5 BEFORE ...e6. The bishop escapes!

lines.title: Exchange Slav: 3.cxd5 cxd5
lines.pgn: 1. d4 d5 2. c4 c6 3. cxd5 cxd5 4. Nc3 Nf6 5. Bf4 Nc6 6. e3 Bf5 7. Nf3 e6 8. Bb5 Bd6 9. Bxd6 Qxd6 10. O-O O-O
lines.lineSummary: The Exchange Slav — symmetrical but Black can play for activity with ...Bf5 and ...Nc6.
lines.strategicGoal: After cxd5 cxd5, develop actively with ...Nc6, ...Bf5, ...Bd6. Aim for ...e5 break.
lines.commonOpponentMistake: White plays passively in the symmetrical position, allowing Black to seize initiative.
lines.punishmentIdea: Black develops more actively with ...Bf5 (outside the pawn chain) and aims for ...e5.
lines.hintText: In the Exchange Slav, develop ...Bf5 actively and aim for ...e5 to break the symmetry.

lines.title: Semi-Slav: ...e6 Main Line
lines.pgn: 1. d4 d5 2. c4 c6 3. Nf3 Nf6 4. Nc3 e6 5. Bg5 h6 6. Bh4 dxc4 7. e4 g5 8. Bg3 b5 9. Be2 Bb7
lines.lineSummary: The Semi-Slav with ...e6 — one of the sharpest and most complex openings in chess.
lines.strategicGoal: Play ...e6 keeping the option of ...dxc4 and ...b5. The Moscow/Anti-Moscow lines are razor-sharp.
lines.commonOpponentMistake: White plays Bg5 allowing the sharp ...dxc4 e4 g5 Bg3 b5 Botvinnik variation.
lines.punishmentIdea: In the Botvinnik (...g5 and ...b5), Black grabs space and material. Extremely complex but sound.
lines.hintText: The Semi-Slav is one of the sharpest openings. ...e6 keeps options for both solid and sharp play.

lines.title: Chebanenko: ...a6 System
lines.pgn: 1. d4 d5 2. c4 c6 3. Nf3 Nf6 4. Nc3 a6 5. e3 Bf5 6. Bd3 Bxd3 7. Qxd3 e6 8. O-O Nbd7 9. e4 dxe4 10. Nxe4
lines.lineSummary: The Chebanenko Slav with ...a6 — a flexible modern system preparing ...b5 and avoiding theory.
lines.strategicGoal: Play ...a6 to prepare ...b5 expansion and keep the position flexible. Low-theory approach.
lines.commonOpponentMistake: White plays e3 passively, allowing Black to develop ...Bf5 and equalize easily.
lines.punishmentIdea: After ...Bf5 Bd3 Bxd3 Qxd3, Black has exchanged the bad bishop and has a comfortable game.
lines.hintText: ...a6 is the Chebanenko move — it prepares ...b5 and avoids the sharpest Slav theory.

lines.title: Geller Gambit: 5.e4
lines.pgn: 1. d4 d5 2. c4 c6 3. Nf3 Nf6 4. Nc3 dxc4 5. e4 b5 6. e5 Nd5 7. a4 e6 8. axb5 Nxc3 9. bxc3 cxb5 10. Ng5 Bb7
lines.lineSummary: Against White's aggressive 5.e4, Black holds the c4 pawn with ...b5 leading to sharp play.
lines.strategicGoal: After 5.e4, play ...b5 to hold the extra pawn. Accept the sharp complications that follow.
lines.commonOpponentMistake: White pushes e5 but Black's ...Nd5 is well-placed and ...Bb7 develops with tempo.
lines.punishmentIdea: After ...b5 and ...Nd5, Black has extra material. The complications favor prepared Black players.
lines.hintText: Against 5.e4, hold the pawn with ...b5! It's sharp but Black is fine with accurate play.

lines.title: vs Quiet 3.e3: ...Bf5 Plan
lines.pgn: 1. d4 d5 2. c4 c6 3. e3 Nf6 4. Nc3 Bf5 5. Nf3 e6 6. Bd3 Bxd3 7. Qxd3 Nbd7 8. O-O Bd6 9. e4 dxe4 10. Nxe4
lines.lineSummary: Against the quiet 3.e3, Black develops ...Bf5 immediately since e3 blocks White's dark-squared bishop.
lines.strategicGoal: Develop ...Bf5 before ...e6 (the Slav idea). Exchange on d3 to eliminate White's good bishop.
lines.commonOpponentMistake: White plays e3 blocking their own bishop, and after ...Bf5 Bd3 Bxd3, Black equalizes.
lines.punishmentIdea: After Bxd3 Qxd3, White has lost the bishop pair and Black has a comfortable position.
lines.hintText: Against 3.e3, develop ...Bf5 immediately! White's bishop is blocked by their own pawn.

lines.title: Trap: ...Bg4 Pin Trick
lines.pgn: 1. d4 d5 2. c4 c6 3. Nc3 Nf6 4. Nf3 Bg4 5. Ne5 Bh5 6. cxd5 cxd5 7. Qb3 Qc7 8. Nxd5 Nxd5 9. Qxd5 e6
lines.lineSummary: A tactical trap where Black plays ...Bg4 and if White gets greedy, Black gets compensation.
lines.strategicGoal: Play ...Bg4 to create tactical tension. If White plays Ne5 and grabs pawns, Black gets development.
lines.commonOpponentMistake: White grabs the d5 pawn with Nxd5 and Qxd5, but Black gets rapid development with ...e6.
lines.punishmentIdea: After Qxd5 e6, the queen is attacked and Black develops with tempo. ...Nc6 and ...Bb4+ follow.
lines.hintText: ...Bg4 in the Slav can be tricky. If White gets greedy with Nxd5 Qxd5, ...e6 develops with tempo.

lines.title: vs London Move Order: ...c6 ...Bf5
lines.pgn: 1. d4 d5 2. Nf3 Nf6 3. Bf4 c6 4. e3 Bf5 5. Bd3 Bxd3 6. Qxd3 e6 7. Nbd2 Nbd7 8. O-O Be7 9. c4 O-O
lines.lineSummary: Using the Slav structure against the London System — ...c6 and ...Bf5 neutralize White's setup.
lines.strategicGoal: Play ...c6 and ...Bf5 to exchange White's good bishop. The resulting position is equal.
lines.commonOpponentMistake: White allows Bxd3 Qxd3, losing the bishop pair and getting a slightly passive position.
lines.punishmentIdea: After Bxd3 Qxd3, White has no attacking chances. Black equalizes comfortably.
lines.hintText: Against the London, play ...c6 and ...Bf5 — exchange their good bishop and equalize.

lines.title: Breyer Variation: ...Nbd7
lines.pgn: 1. d4 d5 2. c4 c6 3. Nf3 Nf6 4. e3 Nbd7 5. Nbd2 Qc7 6. Bd3 e5 7. O-O Be7 8. cxd5 cxd5 9. e4 dxe4 10. Nxe4
lines.lineSummary: The Breyer variation with ...Nbd7 — a solid setup preparing ...e5 central break.
lines.strategicGoal: Develop ...Nbd7 and prepare ...e5 to challenge the center. ...Qc7 supports the break.
lines.commonOpponentMistake: White plays passively with e3, allowing Black to achieve ...e5 with full equality.
lines.punishmentIdea: After ...e5, Black has equalized the center. The position is balanced with active play.
lines.hintText: The Breyer (...Nbd7) prepares ...e5 in one move. Combined with ...Qc7, it's very solid.

lines.title: Dutch Variation: ...dxc4 ...e6 ...b5
lines.pgn: 1. d4 d5 2. c4 c6 3. Nf3 Nf6 4. cxd5 cxd5 5. Nc3 Nc6 6. Bf4 Bf5 7. e3 e6 8. Bb5 Nd7 9. Qa4 Rc8 10. O-O
lines.lineSummary: The Dutch variation of the Exchange Slav — Black develops actively with ...Nc6 and ...Bf5.
lines.strategicGoal: After the exchange, develop ...Nc6 and ...Bf5 actively. Aim for ...e5 or ...Nd7 maneuvers.
lines.commonOpponentMistake: White plays Bb5 but after ...Nd7, the pin is broken and Black has good piece play.
lines.punishmentIdea: After ...Nd7, the Bb5 pin is broken. Black can play ...a6 and ...b5 for queenside expansion.
lines.hintText: In the Exchange Slav, develop ...Nc6 and ...Bf5 actively. Don't play passively!

lines.title: Rubinstein: 4.e3 Main Line
lines.pgn: 1. d4 Nf6 2. c4 e6 3. Nc3 Bb4 4. e3 O-O 5. Bd3 d5 6. Nf3 c5 7. O-O dxc4 8. Bxc4 Nbd7 9. Qe2 b6 10. Rd1 Bb7
lines.lineSummary: The Rubinstein variation (4.e3) — the most popular White response. Black develops solidly and aims for ...c5.
lines.strategicGoal: Castle quickly, then play ...d5 and ...c5 to challenge the center. ...dxc4 and ...b6 ...Bb7 is the plan.
lines.commonOpponentMistake: White plays e4 too early, allowing ...cxd4 exd4 with an IQP that Black can target.
lines.punishmentIdea: After premature e4, ...cxd4 exd4 gives White an IQP. Black targets it with ...Nc6 and ...Rc8.
lines.hintText: Against 4.e3, play ...O-O, ...d5, ...c5 in that order. Then ...dxc4 and ...b6 ...Bb7.

lines.title: Classical: 4.Qc2 Main Line
lines.pgn: 1. d4 Nf6 2. c4 e6 3. Nc3 Bb4 4. Qc2 O-O 5. a3 Bxc3+ 6. Qxc3 d5 7. Nf3 dxc4 8. Qxc4 b6 9. Bg5 Ba6 10. Qa4 c5
lines.lineSummary: The Classical (4.Qc2) — White prevents doubled pawns. Black exchanges on c3 and plays for the bishop pair.
lines.strategicGoal: After a3 Bxc3+ Qxc3, play ...d5 and ...b6 ...Ba6 targeting the c4 pawn and light squares.
lines.commonOpponentMistake: White plays a3 too early, forcing the exchange but giving Black time to develop.
lines.punishmentIdea: After ...Ba6, the c4 pawn is under pressure. ...c5 follows to open the position for Black's pieces.
lines.hintText: Against 4.Qc2, exchange on c3 when forced (after a3). Then ...d5, ...b6, ...Ba6 targets c4.

lines.title: Kasparov: 4.Nf3 Main Line
lines.pgn: 1. d4 Nf6 2. c4 e6 3. Nc3 Bb4 4. Nf3 c5 5. g3 cxd4 6. Nxd4 O-O 7. Bg2 d5 8. cxd5 Nxd5 9. Qb3 Qa5 10. Bd2 Nc6
lines.lineSummary: The Kasparov variation (4.Nf3) — flexible play where Black immediately challenges with ...c5.
lines.strategicGoal: Play ...c5 immediately to challenge d4. After ...cxd4 Nxd4, play ...d5 for central equality.
lines.commonOpponentMistake: White fianchettoes with g3 but after ...cxd4 and ...d5, Black equalizes the center.
lines.punishmentIdea: After ...d5 cxd5 Nxd5, Black has a well-placed knight on d5 and active development.
lines.hintText: Against 4.Nf3, play ...c5 immediately! Challenge the center before White consolidates.

lines.title: Huebner: 4.e3 c5 5.Bd3 Nc6
lines.pgn: 1. d4 Nf6 2. c4 e6 3. Nc3 Bb4 4. e3 c5 5. Bd3 Nc6 6. Nf3 Bxc3+ 7. bxc3 d6 8. O-O e5 9. Nd2 O-O 10. f3
lines.lineSummary: The Huebner variation — Black plays ...c5 and ...Nc6, then exchanges on c3 to give White doubled pawns.
lines.strategicGoal: Play ...c5 and ...Nc6, then exchange Bxc3+ to saddle White with doubled c-pawns. Play against them.
lines.commonOpponentMistake: White accepts doubled pawns without compensation, and Black targets them with ...d6 and ...e5.
lines.punishmentIdea: After bxc3, White's doubled c-pawns are a long-term weakness. ...d6 and ...e5 blockade the center.
lines.hintText: The Huebner plan: ...c5, ...Nc6, then Bxc3+ — give White doubled pawns and play against them.

lines.title: Samisch: 4.a3 Bxc3+ 5.bxc3
lines.pgn: 1. d4 Nf6 2. c4 e6 3. Nc3 Bb4 4. a3 Bxc3+ 5. bxc3 c5 6. e3 Nc6 7. Bd3 O-O 8. Ne2 b6 9. O-O Ba6 10. e4 Ne8
lines.lineSummary: The Samisch (4.a3) — White forces the exchange immediately. Black gets the doubled pawns target.
lines.strategicGoal: After Bxc3+ bxc3, play ...c5 and ...b6 ...Ba6 to target the weak c4 pawn and doubled c-pawns.
lines.commonOpponentMistake: White pushes e4 too early, creating an overextended center that Black can undermine.
lines.punishmentIdea: After ...Ba6, the c4 pawn is under fire. ...Ne8-d6 adds pressure and blockades.
lines.hintText: Against 4.a3, exchange and play ...c5, ...b6, ...Ba6 — target the doubled c-pawns and weak c4.

lines.title: Leningrad: 4.Bg5
lines.pgn: 1. d4 Nf6 2. c4 e6 3. Nc3 Bb4 4. Bg5 h6 5. Bh4 c5 6. d5 d6 7. e3 Bxc3+ 8. bxc3 e5 9. Bd3 Nbd7 10. Ne2 Nf8
lines.lineSummary: The Leningrad (4.Bg5) — White pins the knight. Black plays ...h6 and ...c5 for active counterplay.
lines.strategicGoal: Play ...h6 to challenge the pin, then ...c5 and ...d6 for a solid Benoni-like structure.
lines.commonOpponentMistake: White plays d5 creating a closed position where Black's knight maneuvers are effective.
lines.punishmentIdea: In the closed position, Black's ...Nf8-e6/g6 maneuver is very effective. ...f5 break follows.
lines.hintText: Against 4.Bg5, play ...h6 and ...c5. The resulting Benoni structure suits Black's pieces.

lines.title: Fischer: 4.e3 b6
lines.pgn: 1. d4 Nf6 2. c4 e6 3. Nc3 Bb4 4. e3 b6 5. Bd3 Bb7 6. Nf3 O-O 7. O-O d5 8. cxd5 exd5 9. a3 Bd6 10. b4 Nbd7
lines.lineSummary: Fischer's ...b6 system — developing the bishop to b7 before committing to ...d5.
lines.strategicGoal: Play ...b6 and ...Bb7 for flexible development. ...d5 comes later when the position is ready.
lines.commonOpponentMistake: White plays a3 too early, forcing ...Bd6 but Black has already developed ...Bb7 actively.
lines.punishmentIdea: After ...Bb7 and ...d5, Black has harmonious development. The Bb7 pressures the long diagonal.
lines.hintText: Fischer's ...b6 develops the bishop before ...d5. It's flexible and avoids early commitments.

lines.title: Modern: 4.Qc2 d5 5.a3
lines.pgn: 1. d4 Nf6 2. c4 e6 3. Nc3 Bb4 4. Qc2 d5 5. a3 Bxc3+ 6. Qxc3 Ne4 7. Qc2 c5 8. dxc5 Nc6 9. Nf3 Qa5+ 10. Nd2 Nxd2
lines.lineSummary: The Modern 4.Qc2 with ...d5 — Black plays actively with ...Ne4 after the forced exchange.
lines.strategicGoal: After a3 Bxc3+ Qxc3, play ...Ne4 with tempo on the queen. Then ...c5 for central play.
lines.commonOpponentMistake: White plays Qc2 but after ...Ne4, the queen must move again losing time.
lines.punishmentIdea: ...Ne4 attacks the queen and gains a tempo. ...c5 follows with active central play.
lines.hintText: After 4.Qc2 d5 5.a3 Bxc3+ Qxc3, play ...Ne4! The queen must move and you gain time.

lines.title: Trap: Doubled Pawns Exploitation
lines.pgn: 1. d4 Nf6 2. c4 e6 3. Nc3 Bb4 4. f3 d5 5. a3 Bxc3+ 6. bxc3 c5 7. cxd5 Nxd5 8. dxc5 Qa5 9. e4 Ne7 10. Be3 O-O
lines.lineSummary: After White plays f3 (aggressive but weakening), Black exploits the doubled pawns and weak squares.
lines.strategicGoal: After f3 and Bxc3+, White has doubled pawns AND a weakened kingside. Target both.
lines.commonOpponentMistake: White plays f3 weakening the kingside, then bxc3 creates doubled pawns — double trouble.
lines.punishmentIdea: White has doubled c-pawns AND a weakened king (f3 weakens e3 and g3). Black exploits both.
lines.hintText: After 4.f3, exchange on c3. White has doubled pawns AND a weakened king — exploit both!

lines.title: Romanishin: 4.g3
lines.pgn: 1. d4 Nf6 2. c4 e6 3. Nc3 Bb4 4. g3 O-O 5. Bg2 d5 6. Nf3 dxc4 7. O-O Nc6 8. Bg5 Be7 9. Bxf6 Bxf6 10. Nxd5 Bxd4
lines.lineSummary: Against the fianchetto (4.g3), Black plays ...d5 and takes on c4, keeping the extra pawn temporarily.
lines.strategicGoal: After ...d5 and ...dxc4, hold the pawn temporarily while developing. The Bg2 is blocked by the d5 pawn.
lines.commonOpponentMistake: White fianchettoes but the Bg2 is blocked by Black's ...d5 pawn — the bishop is passive.
lines.punishmentIdea: The Bg2 bites on granite (d5 pawn). Black develops freely and the extra c4 pawn is annoying.
lines.hintText: Against 4.g3, play ...d5 to block the fianchettoed bishop. Then take on c4 for a free pawn.
